newsitem.title: USA: "Sammy Bull" reportedly out of witness protection.
newsitem.headline: "Sammy Bull" reportedly out of witness protection.

text.p: Salvatore "Sammy Bull" Gravano, the gangster whose testimony helped jail Mafia don John Gotti, has left the federal witness protection programme, the New York Daily News reported Friday.

The newspaper said Gravano had undergone plastic surgery on his nose, but this was not considered a disguise because a photograph taken only three weeks ago would appear on the cover of a book about his life story.

The former Mafia underboss entered the witness protection programme in 1995 and has been relocated twice, the Daily News quoted unidentified law enforcement sources as saying. It said he voluntarily left the protection of U.S. marshals about a year ago.
Federal officials declined to say whether Gravano had been let out.
"FBI policy does not allow us to discuss who is or is not in the witness protection programme," an FBI spokesman said in a statement.
Harper Collins, publishers of the book "Underboss: Sammy The Bull Gravano's Story of Life in the Mafia", said it would be in bookstores on April 16.
Author Peter Maas said he had met with Gravano about 6 times during the past 2 years and the former gangster was employed, the Daily News reported. He said he did not know where.
"I would be told to go to City X and when I got there, there'd be a message to go to City Y," Maas said.
Gravano's testimony for federal prosecutors put away Gotti and about 50 other mobsters. He also admitted to participating in 19 murders.
